title: How Charlie Munger Might Invest Today - Shaurya Gupta
description:
📗 FREE GUIDE: Shaurya Gupta's two-page thesis on Alphabet
https://go.good-investing.net/shaurya-alphabet?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=lm-shaurya-alphabet

Shaurya Gupta started his investment firm, Gupta Partnership, at 21. At the first Good Investing Night in Munich he presented three companies that Charlie Munger studied and admired but, as far as we know, did not own directly.

In this talk Shaurya shares his view on:

- His lesson after eight years of running a firm: "whatever expectation I had for an ability to stomach volatility, double that"
- Why Munger disliked the chip business, and why he called TSMC "the strongest semiconductor company on earth"
- Why old chip fabs keep running at full utilization long after they are paid off
- "Find Amazons, not exits": why he sees Amazon as Costco's digital heir
- Alphabet as the company Munger regretted missing
- Munger's story of a woman who bet on the "coming things" with five stocks

The talk ends with an audience question on how he thinks about TSMC's country risk.

Shaurya speaks about companies his firm owns. This is his view, shared for education. It is not investment advice and not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Past performance is not indicative of future results.

summary: The video argues that Charlie Munger would regret missing Alphabet today, positioning it as the 'Berkshire Hathaway of technology' with a strong moat in AI cloud and load factors. The speaker recommends holding a block of Alphabet alongside TSMC and Amazon as a sensible portfolio addition, noting that Amazon and Alphabet together own a third of Entropic. Additionally, Amazon is described as Costco's digital heir and a superior business in the digital age due to its size, growth, and brand strength, while TSMC is viewed as undervalued with strong returns on invested capital.
